question.value: Is the long cyanopolyyne HC5N present in the Class II TW Hya disk, what is its column density and HC3N/HC5N ratio, and what do chemical models say about its formation and emitting layer?

evidence.quote: Here, we report the first detection of HC$_5$N toward the TW Hya protoplanetary disk, representing the largest cyanopolyyne identified to date in a Class II system.
We compare HC$_5$N and HC$_3$N formation mechanisms and analyze the HC$_3$N / HC$_5$N ratio.

referee_caveats_inferred: The detection rests on a 5.3 sigma stack of two lines with individually marginal (3.4 and 4.2 sigma) significance and flux errors near 100 percent for one line
The matched-filter kernel is taken from HC3N, which presumes identical morphology and may bias significance
Column densities depend on an assumed T_rot and an unstated emitting area; HC3N/HC5N ratios span an order of magnitude
Only a single chemical model family at three C/O values is compared, with no fit
No independent confirmation (e.g. additional HC5N transitions) is presented

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several tens of GB of raw/calibrated data for seven Band 3 execution blocks (7 EBs, 325 min on source, 7 spectral windows)
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code and main settings (calibrators, pipeline/CASA versions, beam, rms, GoFish geometry, T_rot range) are given, but self-calibration and imaging parameters, matched-filter implementation and emitting area are not, and the model code is not released.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data public status is not stated and key self-calibration, imaging and column-density inputs are missing, so the 5.3 sigma detection and Table 2 values could not be redone exactly from the text alone.
